behavior.arguments: rdi points at one qword; rsi points at a 20-byte input block; a GOT slot at 0x576e3e0 points at a 16-byte key table (k0 at table+0, k1 at table+8; both runtime values, never claimed as constants). The window returns lo(T * k0) ^ hi(T * k0), where T = lo1 ^ lo2 ^ hi1 ^ hi2 ^ 0x14 folds the hi/lo halves of two unsigned 128-bit products.

edges.final_fold: T = lo1 ^ lo2 ^ hi1 ^ hi2 ^ 0x14, then one unsigned multiply by k0 and a hi/lo fold; the 0x14 survives even when both products are zero.
edges.overlapping_qword_reads: All four input loads are 64-bit qwords at rsi+0, +4, +8, +12, so the window reads a 20-byte span with overlapping windows, not four disjoint fields.
edges.zero_inputs_unit_key: block all zero, rdi qword 0, k0 1, k1 0 -> 0x14 (both products zero, fold leaves 0x14, times k0 1, hi/lo fold 0x14).
edges.zero_key: k0 0 -> result 0 regardless of inputs (final multiply by zero, hi/lo fold zero).

behavior.entry_shape: Opens without endbr64 (first instruction is the rip-relative key-table pointer load); no branches, no calls: mov rcx,[rip+0x1dd1dd9]; mov r9,[rcx]; mov rax,[rsi+0xc]; xor rax,r9; mov r10,[rsi]; mov rdx,[rsi+8]; xor rdx,[rcx+8]; mul rdx; mov rcx,rax; mov r8,rdx; mov rax,[rsi+4]; xor rax,r9; xor r10,[rdi]; mul r10; xor r8,rdx; xor rax,rcx; xor rax,r8; xor rax,0x14; mul r9; xor rax,rdx; ret.
behavior.return_rule: rax = lo(T * k0) ^ hi(T * k0), where (lo1,hi1) = (qword[rsi+12] ^ k0) * (qword[rsi+8] ^ k1) mod 2^128, (lo2,hi2) = (qword[rsi+4] ^ k0) * (qword[rsi] ^ [rdi]) mod 2^128, T = lo1 ^ lo2 ^ hi1 ^ hi2 ^ 0x14. All multiplies are unsigned 64x64->128 (mul, not imul). No field is written, and no other register state is claimed.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

emulator_sweep.method: Window bytes decoded with Capstone and executed by a small interpreter deriving every operand from the decode (independent of the rule transcription), over edge keys, edge blocks, 5,000 random cases, and single-bit/single-byte block variations; the GOT slot was modeled as a pointer to a synthetic 16-byte key table. The emulator script is not committed (needs Capstone, not stdlib) and lives in the builder scratch directory.

incoming_pattern_scan.caller_setup: Both callers share the same setup immediately before the call: lea 0x20(%r13),%rdi; mov %rsi,0x8(%rsp). Caller purposes are not claimed.
incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; exactly two sites found, each confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from its caller FDE start. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: No relocation record of any type in any .rela.* section names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries). The key-table pointer is a rip-relative GOT reference, not a naming relocation.

key_table.note: The first instruction loads a pointer from the GOT slot at 0x576e3e0; k0 = [table+0], k1 = [table+8]. The slot and the table are runtime-filled, so no key value is claimed anywhere; the rule is parameterized by (k0, k1).
